prompt: Predict the probability that a loan applicant defaults, and regulators require you to explain each factor's effect.
tells: probability that a loan applicant defaults
why: Binary outcome plus strict interpretability: coefficients map to odds ratios.
trap: Linear regression can output probabilities below 0 or above 1.

prompt: Will a user click this email: yes or no? You need a calibrated probability to rank who to send to.
why: Logistic regression outputs well-calibrated probabilities for binary outcomes.
trap: Ranking needs probabilities, not cluster labels.

prompt: Build a quick, explainable baseline spam classifier on word-count features before trying anything deep.
why: A linear classifier on bag-of-words is a strong, readable baseline.
trap: Spam isn't rare enough here to need anomaly detection; you have plenty of labels.

prompt: Doctors ask: by how much do the odds of readmission rise for each extra day in hospital?
why: The exponentiated coefficient is the odds ratio per unit, exactly the question.
trap: Readmission yes/no is binary; time-to-event isn't what's asked.

prompt: Estimate each applicant's chance of being admitted from test score and GPA, and show which matters more.
why: Binary outcome, probability output, and coefficients that compare factors.
trap: A straight line can predict probabilities outside 0–1.

prompt: A yes/no churn model predicts "no" for everyone and scores 97% accuracy, because only 3% of users churn.
why: Class imbalance: use class weights, judge with precision/recall or AUC, and tune the threshold.
trap: 3% isn't rare enough to abandon supervised learning; fix the evaluation and weighting.

prompt: A model outputs a probability that a transaction needs manual review. Reviewers can handle only 500 cases a day.
why: Rank by predicted probability and pick the threshold that yields ~500 cases.
trap: The model doesn't decide; the threshold you choose does.

prompt: Which page features (load time, image count, reviews shown) are associated with a visit ending in purchase or not?
tells: associated with a visit ending in purchase or not
why: Binary outcome and interpretable effects: logistic regression coefficients.
trap: Association isn't causation; to prove a feature helps, you'd still A/B test it.
